title: Classical guitar
summary: One string is plucked at a time. Five of the six notes have only that string and no A or D string; the E4 page puts all six strings on the one bridge, E4 plucked and the other five ringing in sympathy. The body follows the plan of a 1964 Madrid guitar, not the recordings' Raimundo 118. The attack is too weak in the top octaves, E2 rings too long, and the body's low air tone dies away too slowly, and no cause is yet known. The nylon trebles and the wound E2 pluck a braced spruce top, a rosewood bridge and the air inside, with a computed air load acting on the shell and sound hole. The back and ribs are African mahogany (Khaya) with the listener at 1.524 m on F5, G3, B3 and E4, and the E4 page also carries a spirit-shellac film on the outside; the E2 and Gb4 pages are earlier renders, put back on 10 November 2026 because they score better against the recordings, and have Brazilian rosewood back and ribs with the listener at 1.0 m. G3, B3, Gb4 and F5 also carry viscoelastic bending loss, air loading on the string and longitudinal string modes; E2 doesn't have the last two, and the E4 page, which puts all six strings on the one bridge, carries viscoelastic bending loss on its three nylon strings, air loading on E4's string only and longitudinal modes on G3, B3 and E4. The renders are tuned to equal temperament and the recordings sit flat of it, so most of each pitch gap is the recordings'. The arpeggio and chord add separate renders, which don't exchange energy.
physics_present: The strings: nylon G3, B3 and E4 open, Gb4 and F5 stopped on the B string, and a wound E2 that takes its tension, line mass and bending stiffness whole from Woodhouse's 2004 measurement of one D'Addario set; on the E4 page the wound A2 and D3 from that set join E2, G3 and B3, all five at rest on the one bridge while E4 is plucked
Two polarizations on every string, with 48 bending modes per polarization on G3, 81 on B3, 60 on E4 (24 on each of the five strings at rest there), 24 on Gb4 and F5, and 96 on E2
Tension on the open trebles comes from tuning the model to equal temperament on an earlier card, so no recording sets a value. They sit within a few cents of it on these cards
The string modes above the kept set carry their exact static compliance into the bridge (residual flexibility)

On G3, B3, Gb4 and F5: viscoelastic bending loss from the pack's cited Kelvin-Voigt row, air loading on the string (cylinder-gas-loading 0.3 30 4) and longitudinal string modes (F5 takes the same nylon-b3 pack as B3 and Gb4, the one that carries that row); on the six-string E4 page the viscoelastic bending loss on the three nylon strings, air loading on E4's string only and axial modes on G3, B3 and E4, the wound E2, A2 and D3 transverse only (a measured whole string carries no axial stiffness), which the network admits at 983 complete modes under its 1024 ceiling
On E2: the friction and bending loss factors Woodhouse fitted to that string

The body of the 1964 Madrid guitar in Zimmer and Mores' 2024 plan: a braced Sitka spruce top with its sound hole, a barred back, ribs and a rosewood bridge, with 128 body modes; the back and ribs are African mahogany (Khaya) on F5, G3, B3 and E4 and Brazilian rosewood on E2 and Gb4. On E2 the bridge's wall is drawn from the plan's own section (shell-assembly-h12-bridge-plan.tsv), whose lighter bridge moves the line read in the rendered sound, where the top's first mode couples with the air cavity, from 192.5 to 199.0 Hz (unloaded, before the cavity couples, from 149.6 to 157.9 Hz). The bridge mobility measured on this guitar (Mores 2021, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.4604577, g20: strongest line 198 Hz, air resonance A0 97 Hz; Mores' printed table gives 200 and 98 Hz) tests that reading: the plan-table body's cavity-coupled bridge mobility, read on a reduced card (the wound E2 string, a compact-neck cavity and no body-radiation skin, because the 128-mode body with the skin load does not fit the engine's 1024-unknown harmonic limit), has its strongest line at 203.6 Hz (+2.8 % against 198 Hz) and A0 at 95.2 Hz (-1.9 % against 97 Hz), so the 20 % gap between the unloaded 158 Hz line and the measured 198 Hz is the cavity coupling and not a structural miss. Above 230 Hz the unloaded structural lines of the drawn-table rosewood body, the specimen's wood, lie within -7 to +3 % of the measured ones (231 against 237 to 241, 255 against 269, 297 against 317, 408 against 410 and 500 to 513 against 506 Hz). Gb4, F5, G3, B3 and the six-string E4 page take the same section in a re-drawn table (shell-assembly-h12-bridge-plan-drawn.tsv; G3 comes to it from the first table's wall, 28.0 mm thick and 8.7 mm high) with the bridge where the specimen has it and the string force where its saddle is: the wall's centre is at 337.34 mm on the top, read from the plan's vector drawing of the bridge outline (182.8 by 28.8 mm as printed, +-0.1 mm; the front photograph agrees within +-1.4 mm), and the string force enters at the saddle, 9.67 mm toward the neck from the bridge's centre (the plan's printed saddle slot, 4.7 mm from the bridge's neck-side edge; 5.3 mm in the photograph), on a rigid massless arm. Disclosed: the arm has no mass and no flexibility, and the 22 mm wall is a line clamp in the model, so the top's rotational stiffness under the bridge is a line's. E2 keeps the earlier bridge at 334.54 mm, driven at its centre, until its page posts

Wood constants from the Wood Handbook (FPL-GTR-282), with wood loss measured on other samples: for the Khaya back and ribs of F5, G3, B3 and E4 the loss along the grain, eta_L = 0.0312 / pi, measured on Khaya ivorensis of another density (Laudares et al. 2023), and the other four loss factors a hardwood-median surrogate (Bremaud, Gril and Thibaut 2011); for the Brazilian rosewood back and ribs of E2 and Gb4 the Wood Handbook's stiffness and density, with the anisotropy and the loss factors of African padauk as the surrogate for Rio rosewood (Bremaud, Gril and Thibaut 2011; loss along the grain 0.0048)
A boundary-element air load on the shell and sound-hole port (body-radiation skin, 20-1100 Hz). It changes how the body moves, not how the note is picked up
The enclosed air with a radiating sound-hole neck, whose outer end takes its mass and radiation from that air load

On all six rendered notes: the sound hole's edge loss, an orifice-edge row on the exterior-neck cavity that adds the viscous loss at the hole's edge (Brandao and Schnitzer 2020, eq. 1.8-1.10), frozen at each card's own air-tone frequency. Resistance only: the equal reactance, about 0.6 % of the neck's air mass, is left out. It takes 3.3 to 3.6 dB off the air tone at 300 ms (3.6 on F5, Gb4 and E4, 3.5 on B3 and G3, 3.3 on E2); on E2 it also makes the fundamental decay about 0.14 dB/s faster through the body

A compact receiver at every frequency, on a 96 kHz clock, placed at 1.524 m on F5, G3, B3 and E4: the UIowa guitar page's 5 feet in an anechoic chamber, the centre QTC40 of a Decca tree; the E2 and Gb4 pages, the earlier renders, place it at 1.0 m (authored). The receiver is an exact 1/r on the cards tested (a 0.5 s Gb4 prefix at 1.524 m equals the 1 m prefix divided by 1.524 to within 0.824 LSB, the int16 rounding bound being 0.828, checked 8 November 2026; the E2 render at 1.524 m against its 1 m render divided by 1.524, 0.827 LSB over all 240000 samples, 9 November 2026), so a clip at 1 m is the same waveform scaled by 1.524

On the E4 page: a spirit-shellac film on the outer face of the top, the back and both rib strips (not the bridge wall, the braces or the bars), 84 micrometres thick, with its storage modulus frozen at 1 kHz. Its law is the fit of Laemmlein et al. (2021) to dynamic mechanical analysis of a 1704-type spirit varnish, MEASURED ON VIOLIN SPECIMENS, not on a guitar (E0 70 MPa, Einf 1.89 GPa, alpha 0.330, beta 0.314, tau 0.125 s, density 984 kg/m3); the thickness is Stephens' (2015) sealer of 44 to 45 micrometres plus top coat of 39, measured on a 3 mm Sitka spruce bar, not on a guitar top. The Poisson ratio 0.30, the strain limit 0.001, the relative humidity 0.35 and the storage drift 0.25 are authored closures (no source gives a Poisson ratio). The page does not separate the film from the other changes it carries over the E4 page it replaces (the 11 mm afterlength, the bridge wall at 337.34 mm, the saddle-crest drive on triangle rows, air loading on E4's string and longitudinal modes on the three nylon strings, the Khaya back and ribs and the 1.524 m listener); against the Khaya render of the same card and binary without the coating line (13 of 16 measures inside the loose ruler and 13 strict) only the coating line differs
physics_missing: The other strings: one sounds at a time, so nothing rings in sympathy, and A2 and D3 aren't rendered. The arpeggio and chord add posted clips, with no coupling through the bridge or body and a balance taken from each page's recording

The string modes above the kept set: partials stop at the 48th on G3, at the 81st on B3 and the 60th on E4 (the most the 96 kHz clock admits on each card; 82 on B3 is refused, and on the six-string E4 page 64, 68 and 70 are refused where 60 is admitted; one E4 string alone admits 70 and refuses 71), at the 24th on Gb4 and F5, and at the 96th on E2, which takes the top of the attack with them. On G3, B3 and E4 a faint line above the last partial isn't a partial: the kept modes move together on the bridge's flexibility, an artefact of the cut. The line moves with the cut: at 48 modes on G3 it sits at 11.3 kHz, 32 dB further under the fundamental in the first 100 ms than at 24 modes, and it's still most of what fills 8-16 kHz there. At 60 modes on E4 it sits at 23.1 kHz, above hearing, and at 81 modes on B3 it moves above hearing too, where it doesn't rise above the reader's floor, about 114 dB under the fundamental

Body modes above the 128 kept, and a converged body mesh. The body's resonances stop near 1770 Hz, and 2 kHz is the most the wood packs allow: their moduli come from the Wood Handbook's static values. A no-skin test with 148 modes moved the partials near the cut in both directions, and on Gb4 brought the octave closer through a partial the recording barely has, so more modes alone isn't a fix

The air tone's loss: the body's low air resonance dies away more slowly than the recording's on G3, B3, E4, Gb4 and F5. The hole's edge loss is on all six rendered notes; with it, over 50-160 ms, the recording's air tone still falls faster than the render's by about 34 dB/s on the B3 Khaya page, about 23 on the Gb4 page and about 52 on the F5 Khaya page (each read on the page's own render with a 40 ms Hann window at the air line, 104 to 105 Hz in the recording and the card's 95.2 Hz in the render), and on E2 the air tone sits too close to the fundamental to read the recording's. On G3 and E4 the recording's air tone is under the noise by about 120 to 140 ms while the render's is still well above it. The computed air load on the outside (the skin) gives the air mode a Q about three times the older compact neck model's (78 against 24 on B3, where the recording implies about 37), as on the violin (52 against 19). On the violin the code read finds nothing dropped: the skin's full-space radiation is right and the compact end's half-space radiation was not, so the older, lower Q was partly wrong physics. On the guitar the skin keeps the compact end's flanged mass and puts back 0.61 of its resistance. What else damps the guitar's air mode isn't identified
G3's string: the recording's string is far less stiff than the printed nylon of this gauge, which suggests a different string; no print for it has been found

E2 is one measured set's whole-string coefficients, not its construction: the core and winding are unknown, and its diameter, which sets only its air drag, is a stand-in from another gauge. Its level falls far more slowly than the Iowa E2's on the posted clips. Longitudinal modes are refused on it: a measured whole string carries no axial stiffness, and no printed axial rigidity for the wound EJ46C string has turned up
The nylon's tension loss enters as zero, because the evidence table has no nylon row
The pluck: one point at one station, released from a static force, not measured on the recordings' player. No print gives the place on a stopped note. A finger or nail's width isn't modelled
Finger and fret contact on stopped notes (the fret is a rigid pinned end), and the player holding the guitar: the model hangs free

The string meets the body through an authored penalty spring (100000 N/m), not the saddle's contact mechanics. On Gb4, F5, G3, B3 and the six-string E4 page the spring acts at the saddle's point on the rigid arm; the second polarization's support (also 100000 N/m, along the body's -y) sits on the same wall triangle as the vertical drive, with the same weights and the same arm, on Gb4, F5, G3 and B3 and on each of the six strings of the E4 page, so its offset is zero there and a lateral force at the crest meets the wall through the arm

The body is one 1964 Madrid guitar's plan, not the Raimundo 118. The maker's pages print the 118's scale (650 mm) and its body depth (95 mm at the heel block, 100 mm at the tail), which agree with the plan's printed 94, 101 and 99 mm to about 1 mm; they print no outline, bracing, plate thickness or cedar species. The maker names the back and sides three ways in three dated captures: dyed mahogany (3 September 2011, three months before the recording session, with no word on laminate), dyed sapele (2018) and, in the shop listing of 2020, filed under laminated construction without saying which parts; the card plays African mahogany (Khaya) for the back and ribs of F5, G3, B3 and E4 (E2 and Gb4 play Brazilian rosewood, the earlier renders put back), a choice, not the maker's word: stiffness and density are the Wood Handbook's Khaya, the loss along the grain is measured on Khaya ivorensis of another density, the other four loss factors are a hardwood-median surrogate, true mahogany (Swietenia) has only a loss factor ambiguous by a factor pi, and the plate is solid wood, no laminate is modelled. Each part has one thickness. The neck and heel, blocks, linings, rosette, fingerboard, bridge patch, string holes, back strip and patches, glue and finish are left out

The plan names no bridge wood: rosewood is assumed. It prints no bridge position either: Gb4, F5, G3, B3 and the six-string E4 page read it from the plan's drawn outline of the bridge and the photograph, and E2 still uses a station inferred from the gap between the plan's axis strips, 2.8 mm nearer the neck than the drawn one

The air load stops at 1100 Hz, and the receiver is compact at every frequency, not a boundary-element microphone. UIowa's own pages disagree with its guitar page, and the card does not resolve it: the microphone inventory lists only QTC50s where the guitar page says QTC40, and the post-2012 page gives 24-bit at 44.1 kHz where the guitar page gives 24-bit at 96 kHz

The loaded harmonic response of the coupled performer (the bridge mobility with the strings, cavity and exterior reaction in it) cannot be exported for these cards: the engine admits at most 1024 coordinates plus poles for it (MAX_HARMONIC_UNKNOWNS), and the G3 card is refused at that check after about 190 s, both in full and with its string cut from 48 to 6 modes and its gas and axial rows removed. Only the unloaded structural mobility, which has no strings, cavity or exterior reaction, can be read
Geometric stretching of the string isn't enabled: it's an alternative to the longitudinal waves, with no published coefficient
The output is 16-bit at a full scale of 1 Pa, so the quietest top-band content sits at the quantisation floor

The finish: only the E4 page carries a varnish, a spirit-shellac film whose numbers come from violin specimens and a spruce bar, not from a guitar. A hunt on 9 November 2026 found no measured modulus, loss or thickness of a French-polish film on a guitar. As a check outside the pages' own numbers, the same law on Stephens' (2015) Sitka spruce bars predicts +4.8 Hz across the grain and -6.2 Hz along it, against +5 to +7 and -7 to -11 Hz measured after seven weeks' cure. The film was rendered on six notes, and a page changes only at or above the note's best-ever count (owner ruling of 10 November 2026). Against the render of the same card and binary without the coating line, it lowered G3 (9 and 9 inside the loose and strict rulers to 8 and 8), B3 (12 and 12 to 12 and 11, the odd/even balance leaving its strict ruler, 8.51 to 11.80 dB) and F5 (10 to 9, in the trial of 7 November on the page then live: the fundamental moved by 0.1 cent, the first second came out 1.0 to 1.7 dB quieter and the decay measure left its ruler, 67.34 dB/s against a maximum of 67.14), left Gb4 at 12 and 12, and raised E2 (8 and 5 to 9 and 6) and E4 (13 and 13 to 14 and 14); one render each. Only E4 posts: 14 and 14 against the live page's 14 and 13, with the total distance to the recording 9.573 against 9.832. E2 (9 and 6, level with the earlier page but farther from the recording in total) and Gb4 (12 and 12 against the earlier page's 14 and 14, the loss coming with the Khaya back and ribs the film was rendered on) were put back; G3, B3 and F5 were not posted

Renders tried and put back, and what the pages do not separate. Against the earlier Brazilian-rosewood renders, the Khaya back and ribs lowered E2 (9 and 6 to 8 and 5) and Gb4 (14 and 14 to 12 and 12: the spectral envelope (cepstral) gap went from 13.18 to 17.87 dB, past the loose ruler's 13.41, and the attack time gap from 0.55 to 2.51 octaves of time, past 1.71), left F5 level (10 and 10) and raised G3 (8 and 8 to 9 and 9), B3 (12 and 11 to 12 and 12) and E4 (12 and 11 to 13 and 13). A query of the bridge mobility with the air coupled in, on the Gb4 body in both woods (a reduced system: no body-radiation skin, no axial string modes, a compact neck), finds no lightly damped body line (Q over 100) on either wood and no line near Gb4's own 370 Hz on the Khaya body that the rosewood body lacks; above 700 Hz it finds one body line on the Khaya body that the rosewood body lacks, at 754.6 Hz (Q 50, 14.6 Hz above the string's second harmonic at 739.98 Hz; the printed Khaya loss factors give a Q of 38 to 47). On the Khaya renders Gb4's second partial stands 5.6 dB higher against its fundamental (-11.4 to -5.8 dB) and B3's third partial, at 740.8 Hz, 9.7 dB higher (-20.8 to -11.1 dB), which fits that line without proving it: nothing was moved or tuned, and the Mores 2021 archive lists no guitar named as mahogany, sapele or Khaya backed whose measured mobility could test it. On E4 the changes of the earlier six-string render (the 11 mm afterlength, the bridge wall, the saddle-crest drive on triangle rows and the two opt-in rows, rendered together) took the page from 14 and 13 to 12 and 11 (harmonics-to-noise gap 12.94 to 16.76 dB, past 14.66, and spectral centroid over time gap 1.85 to 6.12 semitones, past 3.55); which of them did it is not separated, and the Khaya wood and then the film took it to 13 and 13 and to 14 and 14

E2, two renders tried on 10 November 2026 and put back. What got worse: the harmonics-to-noise gap, 0.87 dB on the live page, is 6.52 dB with the air loading on the string (89 bending modes) and 2.01 dB without it (96 bending modes), and the partial decay rate gap, 7.36 dB/s on the live page, is 9.32 dB/s with the air loading and 9.39 dB/s without it; the total distance to the recording rose from 22.006 on the live page to 23.400 with the air loading and to 22.959 without it. Both keep the live page's 9 of 16 measures inside the loose ruler and 6 inside the strict one, the best-ever count for E2 (the page of 5 November 2026), so under the owner's ruling of 10 November 2026 (a tie posts only if the total distance does not grow) neither posts. Both render the live card with the changes the other five notes carry: the string row's length 0.680 to 0.661 m and its bridge station 0.9558823529411764 to 0.983358547655068 (the measured 11 mm afterlength), the translational-bridge row on triangle 131 of the drawn bridge wall (337.34 mm, the saddle crest 9.67 mm toward the neck on a rigid massless arm) in the Brazilian-rosewood drawn-table body, the pluck station 0.779411 to 0.801815 (0.120 m from the saddle, as before) and the receiver at 1.524 m. The first keeps the live page's 96 bending modes per polarization and adds no row; the second adds the air loading of the other notes (cylinder-gas-loading 0.3 30 4, whose one E2-specific input, the string diameter, is the declared EJ46 stand-in of 0.559 mm from another gauge, Anderson and Beausoleil 2024) at 89 bending modes, the most the network admitted under its 1024-coordinate ceiling (the network then counted 129 + 10 n coordinates for n bending modes, so 90 modes were refused). Their control, the live card cut to 0.5 s on the same binary, equals the render of that card by the binary of the live page byte for byte. The fundamental frequency gap stays at 38.2 to 38.6 cent and the partial decay rate stays outside its loose ruler on all three pages; seven measures are outside the loose ruler on each of them.
